thesis: Intel's own Q4 2026 outlook (late October) was weak enough to trigger one of the worst single-day drops in its history (~28%), with management citing component/memory shortages delaying PC purchases and a factory shutdown expected to cost ~$600M of revenue across Q4 2026 and Q1 2027; the stock fell another 10.3% on Nov 5 and is down ~43.5% over 60 days, now trading below the position's average cost. The guidance cut is company-disclosed, but the Nov 5 leg coincided with a broad AI/semis selloff, so company-specific and macro factors are both contributing and neither is clearly dominant. Even with the U.S. government stake and a still-positive 12-month return as counterweights, the disclosed revenue hit extending into Q1 2027 suggests the near-term fundamental picture no longer supports holding.
invalidation: Intel reaffirms or raises Q4/Q1 outlook (e.g., shutdown resolved early or supply constraints easing) and the stock reclaims its pre-guidance range
sources: D&O Diary (Delaware derivative complaint, no scheduled ruling found): https://www.dandodiary.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/893/2026/03/2452000-2452009-https-cl-de_chancery-78689748-101631075.pdf
Insurance Journal (2024 securities suit dismissed with prejudice): https://amp.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2025/07/25/833185.htm

thesis: Marvell agreed on Nov 2 to acquire Lumentum in a ~$115B all-stock deal (4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share; Marvell holders ~67% of the combined company), a pending equity issuance that triggers dilution_risk. The stock is down ~34.5% over 60 days, with drops tied both to the deal and to the broad Nov 5 AI selloff (no company news that day). Management's guide for ~75% YoY data center growth is a plausible positive, but the fixed exchange ratio, $5.8B break fee, plaintiff-firm merger probes, and fiscal Q3 earnings expected later in November leave the read unresolved — mixed evidence rather than a clear net deterioration, so holding is still marginally supported at low conviction.
invalidation: Fiscal Q3 results/guide miss the ~75% data center growth framing, or deal terms/regulatory path deteriorate further

thesis: Oracle registered $10B of common stock and $10B of senior notes in early November (a disclosed equity raise within ~90 days, triggering dilution_risk), and shares are down ~20% over 60 days amid capex and free-cash-flow pressure from its AI infrastructure build. A securities class action over AI-spending disclosures is pending in D. Del. with no scheduled hearing found. Counterweights include management's long-term outlook for a return to positive FCF and analyst targets far above the current price, so the evidence is mixed rather than a clear break; the position sits near its average cost, and the Dec 14 earnings report is the next real test.
invalidation: Dec 14 earnings show further FCF deterioration or additional equity issuance beyond the registered $10B

thesis: Apple's fiscal Q4 2026 report (Nov 2) beat expectations with ~$114.5B revenue and gross margin expanding to 47.9% from 47.2% a year earlier; the stock trades within ~1.9% of its 52-week high. The strongest counter-evidence is management's warning that rising memory-chip costs will pressure holiday-quarter margins, which knocked shares ~3% after hours — but even with that guided pressure, the reported year-over-year margin expansion and revenue beat suggest the underlying business is absorbing cost inflation rather than breaking down. The DOJ antitrust case has no trial date (fact discovery runs to ~May 2027) and no binary catalyst falls before the late-January report.
invalidation: Holiday-quarter guidance is cut or gross margin contracts year over year at the January report
sources: The Next Web (DOJ settlement talks, no trial date): https://thenextweb.com/news/apple-doj-antitrust-settlement-talks-iphone

thesis: James Hardie traded ~10.7x its 30-day average volume today while slipping ~3%, and this run could not identify the cause. Its Nov 5 report beat and lifted the cash target, but coverage notes the reaffirmed guide embeds a softer second half and sharply lower third quarter as the housing outlook deteriorates — mixed rather than a clear net positive. An Australian shareholder class action over pre-AZEK-merger disclosures is pending (no scheduled ruling found). An unexplained volume spike against a weakening end market suggests avoiding for now.
invalidation: Housing demand stabilizes and management raises full-year guidance

thesis: Dropbox traded ~7.3x its 30-day volume today with the price roughly flat. Its Q3 2026 (Nov 5) beat on buyback-aided EPS and raised FY26 guidance, and it agreed to buy Tigris Data for ~$350M cash to push into AI infrastructure — but revenue is roughly flat YoY, the 2027 preview is flat, and analyst consensus leans Sell. The evidence is mixed, with growth resting on an unproven AI pivot, so this suggests avoiding a new entry.
invalidation: Revenue returns to sustained growth driven by AI products/Tigris

thesis: First Advantage fell ~8–10% today on ~7x average volume after Silver Lake priced a 15M-share secondary at $21.80 (below its August $22.20 sale), with up to 5.3M more shares going to Silver Lake LPs outside the lock-up. The company receives no proceeds, so the drop is largely mechanical supply overhang rather than a fundamental change — its Nov 5 report was a beat-and-raise, though bookings and international showed cracks. Continued sponsor selling suggests avoiding until the overhang clears.
invalidation: Overhang absorbed (shares hold above the $21.80 offer price) and growth continues into 2027

thesis: SK hynix ADRs are down ~31.8% over 60 days (listed in July, so the 200-day trend check could not be applied). This run found no company-specific November disclosure; the decline appears tied to sector-wide memory-cycle and AI-capex concerns plus the broad early-November semis selloff, alongside a lingering ADR premium to Seoul shares. A macro/sector-driven drawdown without a company catalyst suggests staying out until a fundamental signal emerges.
invalidation: Company reports or guides to sustained HBM pricing/volume strength and the ADR stabilizes

thesis: P&G is up ~15.9% over 60 days and trades ~1.1% below its 52-week high; Trefis notes it returned 13.8% in the month to Nov 5 while the S&P 500 lost 5.7%. This run found no fresh company-specific disclosure driving the move — it reads as a defensive rotation into consumer staples during the tech selloff, a sector/macro-wide catalyst. No litigation or governance issues surfaced.
invalidation: Risk-on rotation reverses and the stock loses its recent relative strength, or the next quarterly report shows organic sales slowing

thesis: Lilly's Q3 2026 report (Oct 29) showed revenue of ~$24.4B (+39% YoY) driven by Mounjaro/Zepbound and raised full-year revenue guidance to $91–92B from $85–87B; shares are up ~26.6% over 60 days and sit ~1.4% below the 52-week high. The strongest counter-evidence is that oral GLP-1 Foundayo's $184M missed consensus and reported EPS guidance was trimmed — but that trim stems from one-time acquired IPR&D charges (~$4.57/share) rather than operations, and Foundayo is a small fraction of a quarter where the core franchise beat broadly, so neither changes the read. Compounder litigation has been going Lilly's way and no scheduled ruling or trial was found within ~90 days; 2027 guidance comes in January.
invalidation: Tirzepatide demand or pricing weakens materially, or January 2027 guidance implies sharp growth deceleration

thesis: Fox reported fiscal Q1 2027 (Nov 2) revenue of $4.57B (+22% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.54 vs ~$2.02–2.08 expected, with advertising +47% and management saying ad trends remained healthy into fiscal Q2; volume today ran ~5.3x the 30-day average. The plausible negative is that much of the ad surge came from non-recurring World Cup and political spending, which limits how much of the beat carries forward. Smartmatic's defamation suit against Fox has no trial date found within ~90 days.
invalidation: Fiscal Q2 advertising decelerates sharply as event/political spend rolls off, or an adverse Smartmatic development

thesis: LifeStance is up ~12.6% over 60 days with volume ~5x its 30-day average and shares ~7% below a 52-week high set Nov 5, but this run could not confirm a company-disclosed November catalyst explaining the volume (no take-private or deal announcement found). Prior context includes a May 2026 sponsor secondary (no company proceeds) and an earlier Hindenburg short report (not a confirmed finding). Without an identifiable catalyst, the move can't be distinguished from flow/technical activity, which suggests avoiding.
invalidation: A confirmed company-specific catalyst (guidance raise, transaction) explains the volume and price strength

thesis: Costco's company-reported October sales showed total comps +11.1% (+7.3% ex gas/FX) and U.S. comps +12.6%, with nine-week net sales up 12.8% to $54.52B; shares are up ~17.8% over 60 days and within ~2.8% of the 52-week high. The main plausible negative is valuation (P/E ~51) after the run, which this sales data does not directly resolve. Tariff-related litigation (Costco's refund suit vs. the government and a customer class action over pass-through) has no scheduled ruling found within ~90 days.
invalidation: Monthly comps decelerate meaningfully (e.g., ex-gas/FX comps below ~5%) or Q1 FY27 margins disappoint

thesis: Home Depot is up ~14.5% over 60 days, but this run found no company-disclosed catalyst behind the move — the last report (Aug 18) was a beat-and-reaffirm followed by negative drift, and Q3 results are still pending in mid-November, an unresolved binary event. The rally looks consistent with a sector/macro rotation rather than company-specific news, while a peer (James Hardie) just described a deteriorating housing outlook and HD faces multiple tariff-pricing class actions (MDL consolidation contested, no scheduled ruling found). This suggests waiting for the Q3 print rather than entering.
invalidation: Q3 results show re-accelerating comps with raised guidance

thesis: Visa's fiscal Q4 2026 delivered adjusted EPS of $3.48 (+17%) on $12.1B revenue (+13%), modestly above consensus, with FY27 guidance for low-double-digit revenue growth; shares are up ~14% over 60 days and ~4.4% below the 52-week high. A plausible negative is management's flag on higher incentive costs with ~25% of payments volume up for renewal in FY27, and the post-earnings reaction was flat, so the counter-case is named but not fully resolved. The DOJ debit antitrust case has discovery running into early 2027 with trial likely 2027–2028 — no scheduled ruling within ~90 days.
invalidation: Incentive-cost pressure drives guidance below low-double-digit revenue growth, or adverse DOJ case developments

thesis: McDonald's Q3 2026 (Nov 4) delivered adjusted EPS of $3.57 (+11%) and global comps +1.5%, ahead of estimates, and the stock rose ~5% intraday; it is up ~11.7% over 60 days. However, the evidence is mixed: U.S. comps fell 0.2% (first decline after five quarters of growth), revenue missed ($7.16B vs $7.29B), management is not forecasting Q4 improvement, and the gross-opening target was trimmed. Ongoing litigation (McRib class action, discrimination suits) has no scheduled ruling found within ~90 days.
invalidation: U.S. comparable sales decline deepens or EPS momentum stalls at the next report

thesis: Linde's Q3 2026 report (Oct 29) beat with adjusted EPS of $4.59 (+9% YoY) on $9.4B sales (+9%) and raised full-year EPS guidance to $17.82–17.92; shares are up ~11.6% over 60 days and sit ~4.8% below the 52-week high. The record-sales/margin-slippage concern that hit the stock after Q2 is a plausible negative not clearly resolved by available coverage, and the earnings call flagged restructuring, so this reads as a credible company-specific catalyst without a fully engaged counter-case. No litigation with a scheduled near-term ruling was found.
invalidation: Guidance walked back or margin compression resurfaces in the next quarterly update
